access.edition_or_version: First edition, Herbert Jenkins, 1938 (serialised in The Saturday Evening Post, 1938)

mechanics.premise: Bertie Wooster is pressed by an imperious aunt to recover an object that has fallen into a country house, and intervenes in a friend's engagement, drawing him into an escalating tangle of social obligation.
mechanics.reader_promise: Effortless comic entertainment: an unpanicked narrator, elegant prose, and a farcical plot that tightens rather than merely accumulates gags.
mechanics.opening: A domestic morning interrupted by an imperious summons, establishing the narrator's wry, mock-formal register before the plot thickens.
mechanics.point_of_view: First-person narration by the amiable, under-informed Bertie; comic distance is produced by his refusal to panic and his misjudged confidence.
mechanics.character_system: Bertie (narrator and bumbler), Jeeves (competent fixer), Aunt Dahlia (imperious obligation), and a set of friends and rivals whose schemes collide.
mechanics.conflict_and_stakes: Low material stakes inflated by social dread: an aunt's displeasure, a friend's engagement, an object to retrieve. The comedy depends on the narrator treating trivia with mock gravity.
mechanics.structure: Escalating farce: each solution creates a new complication, so the plot heightens one social game rather than adding unrelated episodes.
mechanics.comic_system: Mock-formal narration, mixed-register diction, scale clashes (understatement and inflated formality), and wordplay; verbal comedy serves a plot engineered as a clockwork mechanism.
mechanics.dialogue: Characterful speech in which status, pomposity, and panic are voiced through diction; the narrator's summaries compress and misread events for comic effect.
mechanics.setting: English country house and London clubland, used as a closed social stage that concentrates farcical collisions.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Elaborate periodic sentences resolved by a short comic turn; allusive and slangy diction in tension; running comic motifs and callbacks.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Genial bafflement -> deepening entanglement -> apparent ruin -> tidy resolution, held throughout in an unpanicked register.
mechanics.comic_escalation: Heightening by complication and repetition of the same social rule, consistent with escalation/heightening and incongruity-resolution.
mechanics.climax: A confrontation in which the accumulated obligations collide and are resolved by the competent fixer.
mechanics.ending: Social order restored; the narrator's misreading is corrected with dignity intact.
mechanics.conventions: Draws on the country-house farce and the comedy of manners while keeping its target diffuse rather than a single institution.
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Raises prose style and narrative voice to the level of the comic machinery, making syntax itself a joke-delivery device.
mechanics.critical_reception: Widely regarded as a comic masterpiece; its prose technique is discussed in contemporary criticism (New Criterion; European Journal of English Studies).
mechanics.audience_reception: Enduring popular readership and adaptations; Jeeves and Wooster remain a cultural archetype.
